first_impression.reaction: Googled 'crete wedding venues' because Crete is one of the places we're weighing up and I'm comparing three planners. The intro skips the 'sun-drenched paradise' stuff and gives me a decision framework: guest count, ceremony type, airport. Jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, then the table, which is basically my spreadsheet with honest blanks. Skimmed the venues that could take our numbers, and read the legal and summer-risk sections properly. Then I noticed the page contradicts itself about which end of the island has the biggest venues, which is the kind of thing I check.

journey.quote: The right area depends on three things: how many guests you are inviting, which kind of ceremony you want, and which airport those guests will land at.
journey.reaction: Practical criteria, not adjectives. Good start.

journey.quote: If you would like a second pair of eyes on the shortlist from the start, book a Wedded Concierge consultation.
journey.reaction: I haven't seen a single venue yet and I'm already being asked to book something. Four bullet points isn't evidence. Pitch me after the table, not before it.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: The table runs east to west. It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail on its own official pages.
journey.reaction: Good. No ranking theatre, and the blanks are admitted rather than guessed. Makes me trust the numbers that are there.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: Exclusive use is the field most often misread. At Nana Princess it means the chosen room or venue for a symbolic wedding, not the whole resort.
journey.reaction: That's the catch I'd be hunting for, and they've pointed it out themselves.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: A chapel in the grounds does not by itself mean a Greek Orthodox wedding, and a beach does not by itself mean a legal one.
journey.reaction: Exactly the sort of thing a venue's glossy page would let you assume. Useful.

journey.quote: Seven venues here, from the largest banquet spaces on the island to an adults-only peninsula.
journey.reaction: Hang on. Your own table says Elounda Bay Palace tops out at 500 and Avra Imperial in the west takes 680, and later you call Avra 'the largest published capacity on this list'. So which is it? Once I catch one contradiction I start rechecking every other number.

journey.quote: The east, around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos, has the largest resorts and chapels and is about 50 minutes from Heraklion Airport.
journey.reaction: Same problem again in the FAQ, which is the first place I read. The east venues don't publish room counts, and the biggest room count on the page (Euphoria, 344) and the biggest hall (Avra, 680) are both in the west. 'Largest' isn't backed by anything here.

journey.quote: The largest figures are outdoor ones, so plan a wet-weather fallback around the indoor number for the space you choose.
journey.reaction: 430 outdoors means nothing if it rains. A salesperson wouldn't point that out.

journey.quote: Ask how the 2026 works affect your date if you are marrying next season.
journey.reaction: Flagging building works at a venue you're listing. That's honest about a downside.

journey.quote: These terms come from the 2025-2026 brochure, so have them confirmed for a 2027 date.
journey.reaction: A date on the figures. I can check that, and they're telling me the shelf life.

journey.quote: Adults only is a decision, not a detail. If nieces, nephews or godchildren are on the list, this one is out.
journey.reaction: Blunt and useful. Rules something out instead of selling it.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use, curfew and minimum nights in writing for any venue on this coast.
journey.reaction: I've now read some version of this line five or six times, once after nearly every area. Once is a service description. Six times is a sales script, and it starts to read like the blanks were left there to sell the advisor.

journey.section: Getting to Crete for your wedding
journey.quote: Booking guests into the wrong airport is the costliest mistake on Crete.
journey.reaction: Costliest compared to what? The three-hour drive figure underneath makes the point fine on its own. The superlative is marketing.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that wildfires occur in Greece in the extended summer period from June to September, including near tourist areas on the islands, and can prompt evacuations, and that heatwaves are frequent over the summer months.
journey.reaction: Named source, real risk, not buried. Most wedding sites would leave this out entirely.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens witnesses CNI applications, issues CNIs and witnesses notices of intended marriage, by appointment, with CNIs ready for collection within two working days.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, and linked to the Embassy. That's the standard I want.

journey.section: Shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me how the fee's worked out or whether the venues pay you as well.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and does that affect which ones the Wedded Advisor pushes?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what does it cover?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I get from it?
Is there a real Crete wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: Seven venues here, from the largest banquet spaces on the island to an adults-only peninsula.
turn_offs_found.why: The page's own figures put the largest space (Avra Imperial, 680) in the west, and it says so in the Avra section. A 'largest' claim that the same article contradicts is exactly what makes me distrust the rest.

turn_offs_found.quote: The east, around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos, has the largest resorts and chapels and is about 50 minutes from Heraklion Airport.
turn_offs_found.why: No east venue publishes a room count, and the biggest published room count and hall are both in the west. 'Largest resorts' has nothing behind it, and it's in the FAQ, which I read first.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like a second pair of eyes on the shortlist from the start, book a Wedded Concierge consultation.
turn_offs_found.why: It comes straight after four bullet points and before any venue detail. You haven't shown me anything yet, so asking me to book feels like the sale comes first.

turn_offs_found.quote: Booking guests into the wrong airport is the costliest mistake on Crete.
turn_offs_found.why: A superlative with no comparison or number. The three-hour drive fact right after it is more persuasive than the claim.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the table and the adults-only point, since we have nieces coming
My dad, the wildfire and heat section and the CNI paragraph

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: Most of the page earned it: dated figures, honest blanks, downsides named, risks sourced. Two things hold me back. First, the page contradicts itself about where the largest venues are, so I'd recheck the numbers before trusting the rest. Second, the same old question: do you take a cut from the venue? The fee-in-writing line helps, but it doesn't answer that.

top_3_changes: Fix the 'largest' contradiction (must-fix): the Elounda intro says 'the largest banquet spaces on the island' and the FAQ says the east 'has the largest resorts', but the page's own figures put the largest (Avra Imperial, 680) in the west. Make both match the published numbers.
Move the first Wedded Concierge link below the comparison table, and cut the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' lines from six to one or two.
Drop 'the costliest mistake on Crete' and let the three-hour drive figure make the point. (Commission and fee-model detail would also help, but that's a deferred business detail, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, checked numbers against each other, looked for catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: The 'largest' contradiction (Elounda intro and FAQ vs Avra Imperial 680) is a factual consistency fix, not a business detail. Is the writer picking this up this round?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'crete wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Crete is a live option, hence high relevance.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
Title '15 Best Crete Wedding Venues' is person-set and deferred, so 'Best' is not flagged.
